question.text: Two particles are simultaneously projected in the horizontal direction from a point $P$ at a certain height. The initial velocities of the particles are oppositely directed to each other and have magnitude $v$ each. The separation between the particles at a time when their position vectors (drawn from the point $P$ ) are mutually perpendicular, is

solution.text: According to the question, Representation of position vectors of two particles (drawn from the point $P$ In two dimension, the position vectors $\mathbf{r}_{1}$ and $\mathbf{r}_{2}$ represented as $$ \begin{array}{l} \mathbf{r}_{1}=v t \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\frac{1}{2} g t^{2} \mathbf{j} ...(i) \\ \mathbf{r}_{2}=v t(-\hat{\mathbf{i}})-\frac{1}{2} g t^{2}(\mathbf{j})...(ii) \end{array} $$ $\because$ We know that, when the two vectors are mutually perpendicular, i.e. $$ \theta=90^{\circ} $$ So, $$ \begin{array}{l} \mathbf{r}_{1} \cdot \mathbf{r}_{2}=r_{1} r_{2} \cos 90^{\circ} \\ \mathbf{r}_{1} \cdot \mathbf{r}_{2}=0 \end{array} $$ Substituting the values $\mathbf{r}_{1}$ and $\mathbf{r}_{2}$ in the above relation, we get $$ \left((v t) \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\frac{1}{2} g t^{2} \mathbf{j}\right) \cdot\left(v t(-\hat{\mathbf{i}})-\frac{1}{2} g t^{2}(\mathbf{j})\right)=0 $$ $-v^{2} t^{2}+\frac{1}{4} 4 g^{2} t^{4}=0($ where, $\hat{\mathbf{i}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{i}}=\hat{\mathbf{j}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{j}}=\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{k}=1)$ $$ \begin{aligned} v^{2} t^{2} &=\frac{1}{4} g^{2} t^{4} \\ \Rightarrow \quad v^{2} &=\frac{1}{4} g^{2} t^{2} \end{aligned} $$ $\therefore$ Magnitude of velocity of the particles, $v=\frac{1}{2} g t$ We know that, separation distance between particles at a time $t$ $$ \begin{array}{c} \Delta x=2 v t \\ \Delta x=2 \times v \times \frac{2 v}{g} \Rightarrow \dot{\Delta} x=\frac{4 v^{2}}{g} \end{array} $$
